must_identify.item: nginx fails to start with an [emerg] unknown directive error
must_identify.evidence: nginx validates its configuration on startup and exits with `nginx: [emerg] unknown directive "proxy_conect_timeout" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:9`, producing exit code 1 and the observed CrashLoopBackOff [6, 7].

must_identify.item: The bad directive is proxy_conect_timeout in the frontend-nginx ConfigMap
must_identify.evidence: the mounted ConfigMap frontend-nginx contains an invalid directive, `proxy_conect_timeout` (missing an "n"), instead of `proxy_connect_timeout`, on line 9 of default.conf [8].

notes: The RCA never states a fix. Its only remediation reference is `kubectl rollout undo` under Not Checked. That would stop the crash loop, but it does not correct the ConfigMap: the old pods still mount the bad config and would fail on their next restart, a risk the RCA understates by calling them 'unaffected'. A reviewer should confirm whether fix_acceptable should be false or null.

reviewer_ai.reviewer: claude-opus-5-5 subagent (AI review, not a person)
reviewer_ai.notes: Agree with the judge. The pod logs contain 'nginx: [emerg] unknown directive "proxy_conect_timeout" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:9', which the RCA quotes, and the ConfigMap shows the typo. The only remediation mentioned is 'kubectl rollout undo' in Not Checked. That is neither acceptable fix, because it leaves the bad ConfigMap in place. Calling the old pods 'unaffected' understates the risk: they mount the same broken ConfigMap and will fail on their next restart.

fix_from_suggestions.reason: Changing the ConfigMap directive to proxy_connect_timeout fixes the root cause, so restarted pods will load a valid config; the rollback is only a stopgap, and there is no explicit restart step.
